title: The 'narrower band' claims (29 percent at 4q, 36 at 8q) are ratios of log-unit widths, while every band the product shows is in simple percent
location: ml/src/loop/backtest.py:204 evaluate width, read by web/src/lib/model.ts bandCut, ModelPage.tsx:43-44,77,291, ml/README.md:5,166
why_wrong: The finding treated a unit choice as a wrong number: the page states the cut beside the two widths it publishes, labelled as log growth units (the target's unit), and 29/36 are exactly their ratios. No metro-mean band is ever shown in percent, so there is no mismatch to correct.
evidence: ml/results seqgru.csv/baselines.csv test width 0.1680/0.2359 (4q) and 0.2078/0.3241 (8q); ModelPage caption 'mean width in log growth units'. Percent-unit ratios from ml/data predictions are 25.3/29.1, a different measure.
lesson: A ratio of widths depends on the unit. Check which unit the claim is stated and displayed in before calling it wrong; asking for the unit to be named is an observation, not a defect.

title: (build half) the map's staged body web/public/data/metros.json.part could be committed or published by the workflows if a build dies mid-write
location: bot/build_map_data.py build -> bot/common.py replace_atomically; .github/workflows/bot.yml and national.yml commit and deploy steps
why_wrong: Once web/public/data/*.part is ignored (the finding's real half, fixed), no path is left. A build that raises cleans up its staged body, since replace_atomically unlinks on BaseException. A build that is killed fails its step, and both workflows run commit and deploy only on success. The commit action's git add skips an ignored file inside a directory pathspec.
evidence: tests/redtest_map_part_build.py green on the current code. It builds with a write that raises OSError or KeyboardInterrupt, checks every step after the build for continue-on-error and status conditions, and runs git add on each workflow's file_pattern in a temp repo carrying this .gitignore. Mutants (no cleanup, pre-fix .gitignore, always() on the commit step) each turn it red.
lesson: A leftover from a killed run reaches a commit only if the job outlives the kill and the add picks the file up. Before reporting one as committable, check the step conditions and how the commit action adds files. Here the ignore rule was the whole defect.
